title: Go concurrency for interviews
summary: Goroutines, channels, locks and the memory model; context, bounded concurrency, leak-free pipelines, vendor fan-out under budgets, graceful shutdown, and testing concurrent code for machine-coding rounds.

labs.title: Size-or-time batcher with backpressure and idempotent Close
Generic sharded concurrent map with atomic Update
errgroup clone: WithContext, Go, TryGo, SetLimit, Wait
Cancellable pipeline stages: Generate, Map, MapOrdered, Merge
Vendor fan-out with timeouts, deadline, concurrency cap and partial-result policy

outcomes.text: Predict the behaviour of short concurrent Go programs: output, deadlock, panic vs fatal error, race.
Explain the G/M/P scheduler model and when goroutines cost OS threads.
Choose between channels, mutexes, RWMutex, atomics, sync.Map and sharding for a sharing pattern, and say when the answer flips.
Explain happens-before in the Go memory model and what the race detector can and cannot find.
Implement a size-or-time batcher and a sharded concurrent map that pass go test -race with no leaks.
Propagate cancellation and deadlines with context, and budget per-call timeouts inside an overall deadline.
Implement bounded concurrency, leak-free pipelines and a vendor fan-out with an explicit partial-results policy.
Design a graceful shutdown sequence that fits a platform's termination grace period.
Test concurrent code deterministically and narrate a component's concurrency safety in a machine-coding round.
Benchmark locking strategies and explain contention vs cache-coherence costs.
